utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That would be next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4290, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go back now to page 120 in the hard copy, 130 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, this is a picture of the three buildings that we just referred to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you know, are all those buildings still there today, or --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think so. The only one that could deserve total destruction maybe would be this older hangar, but the rest is most certainly in use. It's -- it's a panorama reconstructed, in fact. When you enter the yard behind the Vuk Karadzic school, this shows roughly what you would see. The back of the main school building at the left, the gym after that, the white -- the white part of it, the side of a gym, the hangar, and the so-called "old school."

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Some witnesses sometimes refer to a stadium or a playground in Bratunac. Is that the same thing as the soccer field?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think so. I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Very briefly let's look at the next image, page 121 in hard copy, 131 in e-court. Now, this -- this is an aerial image that doesn't have a date on it. Who removed the date from this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but the reason why probably the date was taken away is because this one was initially used to mark -- well, both the complex -- the school complex area and the line of buses as they were during the night between the 13 and the 14. So though buses can be seen on this photograph, that is of -- therefore probably dated 12 or 13, but the goal was not to show where the buses were on the photo but where they were later once all the prisoners were regrouped in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So those -- the three red lines just represent where buses were, not specifically on this image, but on the night of 13 July and the circle is the Vuk Karadzic school complex?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's move to another area, page 122 and 132 in e-court. Can you tell us where the next series of photos relate to.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the start of the following phase because we went through the execution sites in the area that we call the area south which is, in brackets, the non-organised killing process that occurred during the day of the 13, and now we enter the area north where the really thorough, well-organised extermination takes place during the days of 14 July, 15, and 16 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. So where's the specific site we're going to look at next?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one is the area of Orahovac where the first convoy of prisoners that left Bratunac town, because one thing we did not say yet is that after the -- the executions of the 13 July all the people who were on the blue spots, the regroupment of prisoners, all of them were then transported to Bratunac town. The reason why at the end of the day of the 13 Bratunac town was completely jammed with these prisoners either in hard facilities or in lines of buses and trucks because all these hard facilities were full. And after around midnight, between 13 and 14 July, the first columns of buses shipped all these prisoners towards the area north where the security officers had the day before spotted detention sites and close-by execution sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm going to object. I think the testimony is going far beyond the perimeters of the Appeals Chamber decision. This witness is summarising a lot of evidence he -- that has been received by the OTP by witnesses, not testifying to things out of his own knowledge. I think it's legitimate for him to depict any site that he would like to do that and explain to the Chamber in general why he is depicting that site, but to be telling us about exterminations, the involvement of security officers and the like is simply something that should be done by witnesses themselves either through live testimony or admission of their evidence under Rule 92 bis. And under the Milosevic case decision, I think he's going too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If I can respond to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. But could you not simply rely on the Chamber's commitment that it will not rely on this witness to find the substantive matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We appreciate that commitment, but I would imagine that you had the same commitment in the Milosevic case and the Appeals Chamber said that the testimony is inadmissible, so it seems to be a matter of admissibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, Mr. Ruez is different from the Barney Kelly case. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I was just going to say that, Mr. President. I actually have copies of their decision here because I thought this might come up. This situation is fundamentally different from the Milosevic situation where an investigator was summarising witness statements and then putting them before the Chamber, and there was no intention to bring the underlying statements before the Chamber in this case. And as you've seen, we've made an effort to refer back to the witnesses who Mr. Ruez is relying on, and I think in the Milosevic appeal decision the Appeals Chamber actually said the basic issue was whether the material itself that was being summarised was itself admissible. That was really the issue and whether the Defence would have an opportunity to challenge that underlying evidence. In this case, they certainly will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But in any event, when Mr. Ruez said that the security officers chose that or pointed out the position, I think it was a bit of a stretch. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Mitchell, when you made reference to the exterminations, I think this might be one of the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I take your point, Judge. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we'll just stick to -- we'll go straight to the site and start talking about some of the findings of your investigation. If we can go to page 123 in the hard copy, 133 in e-court. And before you tell us about this photo, can you describe what was the first -- or the information that first led you to investigate this site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we had a description of a school nearby Zvornik that had a gym and that was close to a railroad line. We had difficulties to identify the area since on the available maps we didn't have the railroad line, but with the assistance of someone in Tuzla, we ended up with a map and could spot this place. After having been there for the first time, we could show the photographs which were identified by the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And can you just orient us on this specific picture, where the school is, where the gym is, and if there are -- perhaps you can also mark on it the direction of the road we can see just turning out to the bottom left of the photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the -- the school, the road being in front. This is the gym -- labels. The gym. The school. The playground. This is the direction towards the exit site. And this road here leads to the road that goes from Zvornik to Tuzla, the Lasva road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you also just mark the playground that you referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P4291.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, we can see this is referred to as the Grbavci school. Is that the same as what's known now as the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We used the names at the early stages because these were the names we had on the maps we had available, but indeed then it changed and all these places are now under the name of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next photo, please, 124 in the hard copy, 134 in e-court. Can you explain or describe what we see in this photo and what the significance of that particular fence is that you have labelled.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The witnesses told that when they arrived, the busses stopped in front of the gym. They stepped inside by walking along a fence, and before entering they had dropped their belongings on a stack at this entrance. So on this picture you can see the asphalt road being just in front, the school building at the right, the gym at the left and this fence that leads towards the gym. That's one of the characteristics that was later recognised by the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: When you refer to the witnesses, can you see any of their names on that list, and if you can, can you tell us their witness codes?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the witnesses are three of them. KDZ064, the witness KDZ039.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And I understand there is one of them who doesn't have a pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's Mevludin Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go to the next photo, page 125, page 135 in e-court. Can you tell us first what this photo is and what is the significance of the labels "Entrance" and "Exit."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When entering the gym, the people step inside through the door that is marked "Entrance." They were then brought to sit in this gym in rows, each row having the back against the previous row, and at the moment they started to bring the people to the execution site the little groups, because it was with the little TAM trucks of little group by little group, they were led through this exit door that leads first to a wardrobe area where they were given a sip of water and getting blindfolded, and then there is another exit door more on the right - you'll see it later - from where they stepped inside the TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photo, page 126, 136 in e-court. And if you can just describe both, what's on this photo and the next one, 126 and 127.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. The witnesses say that from time to time if there was a bit too much noise inside the warehouse, prisoners communicating each with the others, those guarding them were -- fired shots in the air. So this is a hole in the aluminum ceiling that shows a hole in this ceiling. The arrow points to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the next photo, just very briefly, 127?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is another shot showing a holes. A hole, a hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So 128 in hard copy, 138 in e-court. Can you describe again what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph that was used to show to the witnesses to check if it matches the description they made of the line of windows inside this warehouse, for those who were oriented towards these windows, others facing the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And did the witnesses confirm that this did match their -- their recollection?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The next page, please, 129 in the hard copy, 139 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a closer shot of one of these windows with holes inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Page 130, and 140 in e-court, please. And if you can describe to us when this picture comes up -- if we can start with the structure in the top left corner.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If you can describe what that is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a photograph with the date on it. It's the 11 April 1996. It was our first visit in order to have a -- a thorough search of the place. The first visit was a very short stop during the mission with John Shattuck in January 1996. So on this one, at the top right we can see the structure of the school. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Perhaps you can actually mark this one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the exit door of the wardrobe of the gym where the TAM truck was waiting to take the people. That's the vehicle. And then driving out, here is an area of rubbish after the cleaning of the school but that was left there. So we went, as we always do, through the piles of rubbish we come across in these spots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, just looking at the door just to the left of where you've written gym, did that change in any day during your subsequent visits to the site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the following visit to this place, this door was completely sealed. But this one of April 1996 shows that it was not sealed before later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you initial this photo and just date it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit P4292.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the next page now, 131, 141 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we take a break now if it is convenient?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It is convenient, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll break for half an hour and resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to introduce Nikola Sarajlic, who is from Republika Srpska, and is working as an intern with our case managers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 131 in your book, 141 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, can you tell us, firstly starting with the big picture, what are the items we're looking at, and where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, as I said there was this pile of rubbish in the courtyard -- playground, sorry, and going through the items we found inside we lined up those of relevance, which were strips of cloth since the witnesses told us that they were blindfolded before leaving the gym, as well as a certain number of shell casings and also a few live ammunition that were found there and that I handed for destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And is that the shell casings we can see in the inset picture in the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the shell casings we found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, please, 132 in hard copy, 142 in e-court. If you can just briefly describe what this photo shows, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one shows various type of cloth, including some, but they are attached to -- it's a piece of track from a tank or a bulldozer or whatever, heavy machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And we can see a date in the bottom right-hand corner of the photo. Can you tell us what that date is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the date of this mission, 11 of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next photo, please. 133 in hard copy, 143 in e-court. If you can describe each of these photos starting with the one in the top left-hand corner with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them are examples of various types of cloth that were found in the area with labels on them so that -- to identify them further once they are turned into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And these all came from that pile of rubbish in the playground in the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All those we found that day came from this pile of rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, was any of the strips of cloth that you recovered from the school analysed in any way?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- after this process since there were many, I made a collection of the various obvious types by texture and colour, and all those were sent to the forensic lab in order to be later on compared with the same type of cloth that would be found in other areas or mainly those found later in the mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, just for the record, Mr. Manning will be discussing those findings in a little more detail in his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, 134, and 144 in e-court. And firstly, can you tell us when this photo was taken, what year?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one was taken not that same year, because this is how it looked like after the April mission. So I can't remember precisely the -- the date of this one, but it's at least the following season.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's significant about it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only thing is that at this point it could not be able to match the testimony of the witnesses, since they claimed having exited the gym through this door. At this moment there had we not been in the place before, it would be hard to think that someone could get out of this door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We're going to look at a short video now of the school, and again same as last time, we won't have any sound, and if you can describe to us what we're seeing in this video. It's 65 ter 40232A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If you can start off by telling us who took the video and when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the video, and it was in 1998. So here is the school first seen from above. This one is not from 1998. It's the first entrance in January 1996. The very first moment we could step inside for a very short moment, just more or less get in and get out. It was during the mission with John Shattuck. So that's where the people entered the gym, the windows on the right, the door at the left from where -- this is the entrance. This is the exit. And at that time there were still cloths inside the gym. That's the -- the rubbish pile was most certainly created after that. Here is already the garbage. So now -- now this one is the one of the April mission. It's a mixture of various different moments. This is the April mission. So these are the shell casings seen on the previous photograph. At this moment Peter Nicholson who filmed the video was counting them. That's why it stays a bit long on -- on the picture. Empty ammunition boxes, some gas canisters, and cloth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd like to tender at that clip, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be admitted as Exhibit P4293.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's move on from the Orahovac school and go to page 135 of your book, 145 in e-court. If you can just describe what's on this picture and explain how you first came to find those two sites marked as Execution site 1 and Execution site 2.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on these two photographs that make only one, this Grbavci school is labelled as being totally at the left of the picture --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, if you want to mark this picture, please do so.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is already marked on it. The arrow points to the Grbavci school that is just at the limit of the frame at the left. On top is the -- the straight line is the railroad, and more at the bottom the asphalt road leading at approximately 800 metres to a left turn of a small piece of dirt road that leads under the railroad, which is at a height of a bit less than 3 metres, with a little tunnel underneath that leads to the execution site, the first one that was used, the site 1, the second site being, in fact, in front just at the edge of the road. Finding this place could only be done with aerial imagery, because it's -- the site is quite well hidden behind this railroad. None of the witnesses could -- could have helped us finding it. Two of them were talking about a distance of drive of a bit more than five minutes. One of them said 20 minutes, but it's clear that the assessment of time at such moments is quite difficult for these people, so we had no real idea of the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Why don't we just bought there for a moment. We'll move to the next photo, and then if you can continue your explanation. This is -- actually, we'll skip over one. Go to page 137 in the hard copy, 147 in e-court. If you can continue your explanation.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's through an imagery request that we could spot precisely where we had to orient ourselves, and as you can see on these two photographs, the road to the school is marked on the left, the railroad, and in this specific area at the 27 July one can see two areas of obvious disturbance of soil. The one labelled LZ-2 is at the execution site 1 which is the one behind the railroad, bottom right; and the one at the top is labelled LZ, 1 but in fact it's the execution site number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: LZ refers to Lazete; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And why are these sites called Lazete?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the name Orahovac came later and on the map we had at that time, the area around Grbavci school was labelled as being Lazete. This is why we gave it the code-name LZ, like Lazete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, page 138 in hard copy, 148 in e-court. This is labelled LZ-2. If you can just briefly explain the significance of the area that the yellow arrow is pointing to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: LZ-2 is in fact execution site 1 since the execution started with those who were taken first out of the gym. Under this railroad which is, as I said, on an elevation nearly 3 metres high is an underpass that then leads to this open area. At the left a wood and at the right a field. I don't remember what it was called or something like this. So it's in this open space that the execution began.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, 139 in hard copy, 149 in e-court. And can you just tell us again, is this the LZ-1 or the LZ-2 site we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is LZ-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what are the yellow markers we can see on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this being a preliminary mission in order to assess the site and determine if there disturbance seen on the picture had indeed a direct relationship with the events that we were looking into, we made a surface check of this area of disturbance, and these markers spot various items being in relation with the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We'll look at a few of those items in more detail now. Can we go to the next page, 140 in hard copy, and 150 in e-court. If you can describe what the object next to the number 25 tag is and what the basis of your knowledge is about this object.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- we were on this mission in company of Bill Haglund, and he is the one who told us what these items, for most of them, were. This one is a human femur, the number 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next photo, please, 141 in hard copy, 151 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 32 is a human jaw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that was identified by Dr. Haglund?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, please, 142 and 152 in e-court. What's the item just in front of the number 17 tag?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a shell casing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next photo, 143, page 153 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we see page 137 briefly again. That's the aerial image. So on this photo Grbavci school should be above the photo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Above. Top right. Direction top right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I was confused with this direction of the arrows, so it -- it didn't move that way. The other way round.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because where the arrow is they never went. But there was no space to put the arrow at the top right because of the marking of two areas of disturbed earth, but I will mark one reference point. The way the vehicles, the little trucks brought the people is this one. To site 1. And at the final stage, it was the site 2. Site 1 being Lazete 2, and site 2 being Lazete 1. But at the time we didn't know about the real chronology of the events. The first assuming was that they first used the most easy place, which is the Lazete 1 and then the more remote one, but in reality it's totally reversed. The survivors all talk about Lazete 2 which is the first execution site and there is actually no survivors from the site -- the second site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you mark the arrow in order to know the direction at the end of that line, yes. No, on the left side. You marked the direction. The head of an arrow. No. "To school." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we mark it as the next exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you just said the survivors all talk about Lazete 2. Are they the three names that you provided earlier?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies. I was told that the Registry just lost the image. Could you kindly do the marking again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Redoing it, no problem. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go back to page 143 in the hard copy and 153 in e-court. And if you can just describe the object to the right of the number 43 marker.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's cloth, one knotted and one being a piece of clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And this is again at the LZ-2 site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is LZ-2, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And next photo, please, 143 -- 144 in hard copy, 154 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just a larger view of -- of items we have shown, one shell casing, the piece of cloth, just to show how the items are spread due to the use of all this heavy equipment. The items on the surface are spread all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next photo, please, 145 and 155 in e-court. First, is this still the LZ-2 site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, what's the significance of the area that's marked by the yellow tape in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this area is most probably the one the witnesses are referring to as a rest area for the soldiers who were executing the prisoners. It's where they were reloading their guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And did you go to the site with any of the three survivors?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: With one of them we -- we went, and this is where we had the confirmation that without aerial imagery, we would never have found the spot even with the witness, since we walked along the asphalt road and he passed by the site without recognising nothing, because from the road you -- you could not see anything there. So we had to then orient him right on the spot so that he could retake his bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you see his witness code on that list in front of you, the particular individual you went there with?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. KDZ064.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the next page, please, 146 and 156 in e-court. Now, can you tell us what the object in this photo is and where it was found?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one was found on the so-called rest area among a few others of these. It's a little -- it's a packaging of -- of rounds, ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recall what type of ammunition the packaging is for?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written on the box. It's for 7.62 calibre ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We can turn it around and zoom it further so that ... We can zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We could zoom maybe a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. 7.62, I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's the most common calibre in use by all the -- the small weaponry in use by the former JNA and all the army forces down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo, 147 in hard copy, 157 in e-court. And again if you can describe what this object is and where it was found.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this -- this one was found at the -- at the top of this so-called rest area. One witness overheard the killers say when they switched from one side to another, Take the ammunition box. And this one was empty and left behind, obviously. It was just at the edge of the wooden area at the top of this rest area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo, 148 and page 158 in e-court. And if you can just describe.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a metal box that contains more than 1.000 rounds inside packaged -- inside smaller packets of paper packets, the ones that we found, for example, on this rest area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And this is the same box we saw in the previous photo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the box that we saw on the round, the small white one, is one of the many who are inside such an aluminum box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: But the box immediately before this box on it's side -- perhaps we can go back one page to 147. So this is the same box?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. This is how we found it, and then I flipped it over to take the photo of what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go back to 148 and just zoom in on the box so we can see the calibre of ammunition it contained. If you could just read that out for the record, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So 1200 -- it's maybe 86 or 66 - I don't read it very well - of 7.62, then it's in Cyrillic, but it's millimetre. It's the calibre of ammunition. And the serial number of the box at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo, page 149 in hard copy, 159 in e-court. And if you can -- well, firstly, this isn't a box that was found at that site, is it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. We found it in a completely different location where we were looking for possible -- possible burial place in a cave where we didn't find any body, but we found an ammunition dump among which was this metal and -- first wooden box, metal box inside and then the little paper boxes, and I used this photograph in order to explain how the packaging is. So the metal box we found is the same style of metal box containing ammunition. On this one it's more even easy to read, and inside are these smaller boxes that contain the rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So this is just purely an example?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's purely an example to show how this packaging is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, 150 in hard copy and 160 in e-court. And this is the LZ-2 site again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And if you can just explain the significance of the red arrow -- or the orange arrow.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in fact again these -- the execution site is here. The -- the rest area we were talking about is here, and this is the underpass that leads from the school to the site, but once the execution here was over, the witnesses said once the -- the entire meadow was full of bodies. This was something for us later important, because when we found the site on the opposite side, it's impossible to figure out that the site could be covered with bodies because it's much too big, but this site, the site 1 that witnesses talk about indeed has the sizes of -- due to the amount of people who were later found could cover the entire area. So after this execution was completed, the killers returned through this underpass to hit the other side of the railroad line that is sandwiched between the railroad line and the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you initial and date this, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo, 151 in hard copy, 161 in e-court. The next page, please, 161. Can you briefly describe this to us, Mr. Ruez. And perhaps to orient us, if you can put an arrow in the direction of where the LZ-2 is, the LZ-2 site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the right is the railroad line that goes towards Zvornik. One of the survivors, after having left the execution site 1, went above this railroad line and walked until he saw the lights and recognised the Zvornik area. Underneath is the underpass, the site 1 being a -- LZ-2 being here. So going underneath. This is the road to the school. So this is the -- the last execution site. Those who were still in the school were taken and just shot on this open area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's the area with the yellow circle?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the area with the yellow circle. This house did not exist in that location during the summer 1995. It was constructed after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could you also mark on this photo the direction the trucks took to get to the LZ-2 site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you initial and date this, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P4296.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, please, 152 in hard copy and 162 in e-court. We're going to see an aerial shot or photo taken from the air of these two sites. If you can just orient us on this picture again.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the -- the school being -- being at the left, bottom left. Direction of the trucks towards the execution site, and then Lazete 1. So on this one it's much clearer to see the situation, knowing that those who survives in this place, except the one who walked the railroad, the others they did hid through this direction, through the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you initial and date that one, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit 4297.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, 153 in hard copy and 163 in e-court, and we'll just move briefly through the next three photos, Mr. Ruez, and come to a video that shows much of the same material?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's some technical problems, but we can save the image from video. We can carry on, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, 153. It's 163 in e-court. Mr. Ruez, if you can just briefly tell us what we can see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a rubbish dump site very close by of the Lazete 2 area through which, as we always do, we went through in order to see if there was any link with the previous site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the next photo, 154, and 164 in e-court. If you can very briefly tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a part of the content of the -- the rubbish dump site. We are in the beginning of the process of going through it. In this place here, in fact it's mainly socks, hats. I mean, personal belongings, let's call them like this. These ones. Clothing. And more interesting also is these ones, but on the video I think you wanted to show -- we can see more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We'll get to the video in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is cloth, blindfold size.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is it possible to save that, or are there problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, if you could initial and date. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P4298.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same type of -- the same colour of -- as the ones that were found at Grbavci school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page, 155 and 165 in e-court. The yellow arrow on the right points to that dump site that we just saw on the previous two photos; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The dump site is precisely here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think we need to mark -- keep this separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No. We won't take this one, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a video now, Mr. Ruez, and as with the last two, we'll turn off the sound and just have you describe what we're looking at. This is 65 ter 40226A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, again, an aerial view of the school and then the road leading to the execution site at the left of it. So we turn around in order to -- to show the distance between the school and the site, but we measured the distance with a true metre. And I think I remember it, it was 800 metres. So here the turn left, going through the underpass, the railroad. So now seen from the ground. The LZ-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recall when this video was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the -- hmm. It was during this first -- this first mission, so I think we had the date on the photos, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We can come back to that. If you --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it was April. It was the mission of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If you could just continue with the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: April 1996. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If you could continue with the description of the image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the beginning of a dig. And this specific mud is created by the decomposition of the bodies. It's green-ish. Makes a clear difference with the normal soil. It's the decomposition that makes the mud be so greenish. A shell casing, clothing. The initial dig was, as you can imagine, not very easy because of the mud, the rain. So we couldn't go really deep in this one, but there were enough items all around to be quite certain that there were multiple bodies underneath. A bone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recall who this is in the footage at the moment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Bill Haglund with yellow clothing and the red rubber gloves. Bill was on these preliminary missions, and it is thanks to his presence that the exhumation process could start at the very early stage, as soon as 1996. That is the area of rubbish where the dump site was found. Behind these bushes one can see the road line -- the railroad, sorry. And that's now the result of the search done in this -- on this site. So at this moment we are describing the items. So these are socks. Describing and counting. Hats. And pieces of cloth. I think there were some 110 pieces left in the dump site. Some of them being without -- without further technical expertise that was done by the lab, but clearly obviously the same ones than those at the Grbavci school, but the connections were made later also with the grave and so on. Dean Manning will be the one unfolding all this. Ammunition, some live, some used. It's a canister of something. Some personal items. Some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that video, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be Exhibit P4299.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're going to move to a completely new site now. I can start if you'd like, or we can start with a fresh site on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's adjourn for today. Mr. Ruez, in order to accommodate the next witness, I was told that Prosecution has decided to interpose his evidence during your testimony, so I apologise on -- on behalf -- for your inconvenience. On Monday we'll start in the afternoon, i.e., quarter past 2.00, and we'll hear evidence of Mr. Haglund. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, what might be easier is Dr. Haglund has to leave by the end of Tuesday, so I can finish Mr. Ruez's direct and then have Dr. Haglund and then Mr. Ruez's cross just so it doesn't get too chopped up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, if that suits you. I take it there's no position from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of January, 2012, at 2.15 p.m.
